source: Synthetic; modeled on a realistic builder mistake. The producer ships a `findActiveForUser()` stub returning null with a TODO, and tests that only assert the method exists — bypassing the verify line's actual behavior requirement.

input.verify_line: Unit tests against Firestore emulator: create → get round-trip; update changes only specified fields; findActiveForUser returns the one incident with endedAt == null && deletedAt == null.
input.diff_summary: IncidentRepository.findActiveForUser is `// TODO: implement query; return null;`. Tests assert only that the method exists (`typeof repo.findActiveForUser === 'function'`).

notes: Two-finding case. Tests the cold-reader's ability to (a) catch a stubbed implementation that lies about completion (CRITICAL/scope_check 1), and (b) catch shallow tests that don't assert verify-line behavior (HIGH/scope_check 2). The cited_section uses the array form because the verify line is testing behavior implied by both BR-26 (singleton) and §5 (data model) — either is a valid cite per the prompt's nearest-BR/§ rule. Demonstrates the multi-acceptable-cite pattern added round 16.
